name: transpose drops what falls off the keyboard
about: transpose moves a note on and its note off by the same number of semitones, and a note that lands outside 0..127 is dropped rather than clamped to the edge.
notes: out note = in note + by. Kept when 0 <= out <= 127, dropped otherwise. Status and velocity unchanged.
l1 to up is by +12, l2 to down is by -12. Within one input the outputs follow link order, up before down.
t 1: note 116 (74). up 128 is past 127 and DROPPED. down 104 = 68. NEGATIVE CONTROL: a clamping transpose would send 90 7F 64 to up, a note nobody played.
t 2: note 115 (73). up 127 = 7F, the top edge, kept. down 103 = 67.
t 3: note 11 (0B). up 23 = 17. down -1 is below 0 and DROPPED. NEGATIVE CONTROL: a clamp would send 90 00 64.
t 4: note 12 (0C). up 24 = 18. down 0 = 00, the bottom edge, kept.
t 5: the note off of 60 with release velocity 40 moves with it: up 80 48 40, down 80 30 40.
t 6: the note off of 116. up 128 is dropped, which matches the note on up never got. down 104: 80 68 40.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 7: CC 60 (B0 3C 64) is not a note, its number is not a pitch, and it passes unchanged to both.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l3 asks for by 128, outside -127..127, and is refused bad-args.
